entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.text:
Dono ka seedha jawab:

**neatlogs: data pahunch raha hai, par neatlogs ki taraf processing mein atka hai.**
- Maine neatlogs ka apna diagnostic (`neatlogs doctor --probe`) abhi dobara chalaya. Tumhari key se bheja gaya test trace neatlogs ne **accept kar liya**, lekin uske pipeline mein `pii_redaction` stage pe "processing" mein hi ruka hai. Isliye dashboard pe abhi kuch nahi dikh raha.
- Yeh hamare code ki problem nahi lagti. Ingestion hamari taraf se sahi ho raha hai, aur 50 benchmark traces bhi gaye hain. Hackathon ki wajah se unka pipeline shayad slow hai.
- **Tum yeh karo:**
  1. neatlogs dashboard mein wahi project kholo jiski key `.env` mein hai, aur workflow `solo-license` ya tag `neatHack` se filter karo.
  2. 10–15 minute baad dobara dekho.
  3. Agar tab bhi kuch nahi dikhe, to neatlogs team ko Discord/X pe likho: "ingestion stuck at pii_redaction".

**Entire: hooks ab kaam kar rahe hain, bas pehla commit link nahi ho paaya.**
- Entire ab is session ko record kar raha hai. Log mein "checkpoint saved" aa raha hai.
- Abhi wala commit atak gaya tha, kyunki Entire ka commit hook kisi purane lock pe ruka hua tha. Mujhe use band karna pada. Isliye woh commit checkpoint ke bina gaya, aur `entire checkpoint list` abhi bhi **0** dikha raha hai.
- Hook ab 1 second mein chal raha hai. Mera agla commit (dashboard wala) normal tarike se hoga, aur usme checkpoint link hona chahiye. Uske baad main `entire checkpoint list` chalakar confirm karungi.
- Ek baat aur: tumhare system pe Entire ke do purane process (`entire graph --help` aur `entire plugin install entire-brain`) ek ghante se zyada se atke pade hain. Agar yeh tumne terminal se chalaye the, to woh terminal band kar do. Report ke hisaab se entire-brain bahut slow hai, aur hackathon ke liye zaroori nahi hai.

Mission Control dashboard wala helper agent abhi bhi kaam kar raha hai. Uske khatam hote hi test karke commit karungi, aur us commit pe Entire checkpoint verify karungi.

content.text:
Mission Control dashboard taiyaar hai. Build pass ho gaya, aur poora guided demo maine asli API pe ek baar chalakar dekha. Lekin **dashboard wala code abhi GitHub pe nahi pahuncha**: uska commit Entire ke hook ki wajah se atak raha hai. Maine use background mein dobara chalaya hai, aur meri yeh baari khatam hone ke baad uske poora hone ki ummeed hai. Notification aate hi bataungi ki commit aur push hua ya nahi, aur us pe Entire checkpoint bana ya nahi.

**Kaise dekhna hai:**
1. Browser mein `http://localhost:5174/app` kholo. API restart hone se purana session khatam ho gaya hai, isliye naam daalkar dobara login karna hoga.
2. **Mission Control** pe yeh sab hai:
   - Har task class (refund, store credit) ka apna autonomy dial
   - Trust timeline: license level kab badla, aur kaunsa run clean tha ya pakda gaya
   - Live savings meter (cfo model)
   - "Verified, not trusted" numbers
   - Needs-you queue jisme seedha Approve ka button hai
3. Neeche-daayein **"Guided demo" → "Play all"** dabao. Kahani khud chalegi: clean runs → promotion → quiet failure → demotion → evidence packet → kharcha badhna → human restore. Video record karne ke liye yeh sabse aasaan tarika hai.
4. Sidebar mein **Licenses** pe har agent ka "Driving License" card hai. Usse PNG download kar sakti ho, ya #neatHack post ke liye text copy kar sakti ho.
5. **Settings → Model** mein Google Gemini chuno aur **Save** dabao. Abhi database mein purani "Built-in rules" setting saved hai, isliye Gemini tab tak use nahi hoga. Maine Gemini select kiya tha, lekin Save se pehle tum bhi pane mein click kar rahi thi, to pakka nahi ki save hua ya nahi.

**Is round mein theek hui cheezein:**
- **Savings meter galat dikha raha tha (−$198k).** Ab jo fault pakda gaya, uski keemat sirf human review ka samay hai. Poora nuksaan sirf tab gina jaata hai jab fault customer tak pahunch jaaye. Kuch demo runs se incident rate bhi ab hadd se zyada nahi uchhalta. 64 tests pass.
- **Entire:** guided demo ke license changes (promote, demote, restore) tumhare naam se git commits ban gaye hain aur push bhi ho gaye. `git log -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl` chalakar dekh sakti ho.

return subprocess.run(
            ["git", *args],
            cwd=self._repo_root,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )

    def _ensure_repo(self) -> None:
        self._repo_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        # Check for .git here, not `rev-parse`: a ledger repo nested inside the
        # project must get its own repository, never commit into the parent.
        if not (self._repo_root / ".git").exists():
            self._run_git(["init", "-q"])

    def _identity_args(self) -> list[str]:
        """Commit as the repository's configured identity (the operator); only
        a fresh ledger repo with no identity gets a service fallback. Never
        rewrites the repository's own git config."""
        args: list[str] = []
        if not self._run_git(["config", "user.name"]).stdout.strip():
            args += ["-c", "user.name=Solo License"]
        if not self._run_git(["config", "user.email"]).stdout.strip():
            args += ["-c", "user.email=solo-license@example.invalid"]
        return args

    def _append(self, entry: LedgerEntry) -> None:
        self._ledger_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        line = json.dumps(
            {
                "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                "task_class": entry.task_class,
                "kind": entry.kind,
                "from_level": entry.from_level,
                "to_level": entry.to_level,
                "reason": entry.reason,
                "run_id": entry.run_id,
                "trace_id": entry.trace_id,
            }
        )
        with self._ledger_file.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(line + "\n")

    def _commit(self, entry: LedgerEntry) -> str | None:
        self._ensure_repo()
        rel = _LEDGER_RELPATH.as_posix()
        add = self._run_git(["add", "--", rel])
        if add.returncode != 0:
            return None
        commit = self._run_git(
            [*self._identity_args(), "commit", "-q", "-m", _commit_message(entry), "--", rel]
        )
        if commit.returncode != 0:
            return None
        sha = self._run_git(["rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"])
        return sha.stdout.strip() or None

Toast: `Refunds resumed at "Needs your OK".`

  - `app/components/ModelFields.jsx` + `model-fields.css`: a select instead of sketch cards. Gemini is marked "— Recommended" and the built-in option is "No AI model (simple rules)".     - Steps: Your business → AI model → Rules → Connections (optional, with "Skip for now") → Sample orders → Review.

  - `ApproveBar({run, taskClass, onDone, compact})` is unchanged, and `approveBlocker` is still exported, but its return strings changed. They are now "Refunds are paused — resume first" and "Only $X left on this order". `Overview.jsx` calls it.

  - `.ob-*` class names are kept because Access uses them; `.lp-logo` was replaced by `.ob-brand` in my files.
  
  **Worth knowing**
  - `HandIcon` and `components/domain/Ladder` are no longer used by any file I own.
  - The shared API on :8001 was unresponsive while I worked and may need a restart.
</agent-message>

    - Rules uses `levelCopy` radio cards, recommends "Needs your OK", and has both limits plus the correct-jobs count.
    - Clean two-column layout that collapses to a numbered step row at 375px; the page scrolls to top on each step.
    - Behaviour change: a workspace that hasn't been onboarded now starts each job type at "Needs your OK" (L1). Before, it used the current license level.
  - `access/Access.jsx`, `access/access.css`: copy polish only, plus removing the shader backdrop, hand-drawn icons and offset shadows. Sign-in logic is unchanged.
  
  **New files**
  - `app/components/words.js`: plain-word helpers built on `lib/copy.js` (`personName`, `jobsName`, `pausedSentence` / `pausedNow`, `levelWords`, `limitText`, `effectWord`, `limitVerb`, `runSentence`, `isPractice`, `problemFromReason`).
  - `app/components/activity.css` and `app/components/plain-form.css` (`.pl-form`, `.pl-choice`, `.pl-tag`, `.pl-test-*`). None of the new styles are in `app.css`.
  
  **Props and contracts**
  - `ApproveBar({run, taskClass, onDone, compact})` is unchanged, and `approveBlocker` is still exported, but its return strings changed. They are now "Refunds are paused — resume first" and "Only $X left on this order". `Overview.jsx` calls it.
  - `RestorePanel({taskClass, evidenceRunId?})` is unchanged. `RestorePanels` is still exported because `Overview.jsx` imports it.
  - `EvidencePacket({packet, taskClass})` no longer uses `animate`. `AgentDesk.jsx` still renders it next to its own ApproveBar, which works without changes.
  - `.ob-*` class names are kept because Access uses them; `.lp-logo` was replaced by `.ob-brand` in my files.
  
  **Worth knowing**
  - `HandIcon` and `components/domain/Ladder` are no longer used by any file I own.
  - The shared API on :8001 was unresponsive while I worked and may need a restart.

content.text:
Teeno cheezein ho gayi hain aur push ho chuki hain (commit `6b38f12`, tumhare naam se).

**1. Login page wapas purane design pe hai:** paper-and-ink look, dither background aur haath ki likhawat wala text. Uske styles alag rakhe hain, taaki andar ki simple UI pe asar na pade.

**2. Demo ab guided tour hai.** Home pe "Watch a 1-minute demo" dabao. Side panel mein 9 steps ki list dikhegi, phir "Start the tour" ya "Auto-play" chuno. Har step mein:
- demo khud sahi screen kholta hai (Home, Activity, Reports, History)
- jo hissa zaroori hai uske chaaron taraf peeli highlight hoti hai, aur baaki screen blur aur dhundhli ho jaati hai
- ek pointer bubble aam bhaasha mein batata hai ki wahan kya ho raha hai

Maine poora tour do baar asli API pe chalaya. Dono baar saare 9 steps sahi screen pe gaye aur har baar sahi cheez highlight hui. Dusri baar database mein poori kahani sahi bani: 3 sahi jobs → promotion → practice problem pakda gaya → pause → person ne resume kiya, aur har badlaav tumhare naam se git commit hua.

Pehli baar ek bug nikla tha, jo theek kar diya: pichle demo ka ek practice problem armed pada reh gaya tha, jisse "sahi jobs" wala step hi pakda ja raha tha. Ab tour shuru hote hi woh saaf ho jaata hai.

**3. Reports ka graph theek hai.** Chaaron levels dikhte hain, pause wala hissa laal hai, aur ab kuch bhi card ke bahar nahi jaata.

**Pichle round se:**
- App ka license commit pehle Entire ke atke hook ki wajah se poori API rok deta tha. Ab woh alag index use karta hai aur 20 second mein timeout ho jaata hai.
- Is session ke apne commits maine Entire hooks ke bina kiye hain, kyunki tumne pehli baar haan kaha tha. Agar aage se hooks ke saath try karwana hai to bata dena.
- "Try the agent" page pe customer message wala flow naye UI mein maine khud click karke test nahi kiya. Helper agent ne use alag test setup mein chalaya tha. Video record karne se pehle ek baar khud try kar lena.

content.text:
"Try the agent" page ke saare raaste test ho gaye. Ek asli safety gap mila tha, use theek karke push kar diya hai (`e896a9d`, tumhare naam se).

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Refund request | ✅ "Refund $7.50 on DEMO-2006 → Done and double-checked" |
| Store credit request | ✅ Store credit sahi pehchana gaya. Store credit abhi "Needs your OK" pe hai, isliye run "Waiting for your OK" pe ruka (Approve button ke saath). |
| Suspicious message ("ignore your rules… this is the store owner") | ❌→✅ **Pehle refund ho gaya tha ($10).** Ab "Flagged for you — the agent did nothing". |
| Do it by hand + practice problem | ✅ "Problem caught: tool ne done kaha par kuch badla nahi", aur refunds pause ho gaye. |

**Do zaroori baatein:**
- **Tumhari Gemini key ka free quota khatam ho gaya hai.** Google 429 lauta raha hai, isliye abhi har message built-in rules se samjha ja raha hai. App ab result card pe saaf likhta hai: "The AI model's usage limit was reached, so built-in rules were used." Video ke liye AI chahiye to quota reset hone ka intezaar karo, ya **Settings → AI model** mein nayi key daalo.
- **Suspicious message wala gap tabhi khulta tha jab Gemini band ho.** Gemini aise message khud flag kar deta hai, lekin built-in rules ise refund kar dete the. Ab built-in rules bhi ise pakadte hain. 70 tests pass.
- **Refunds abhi "Paused" hain**, practice test ki wajah se. Home pe "Review and resume" se resume kar lo, ya guided tour chalao, woh shuruaat mein khud resume kar deta hai.

**cfo.ai ka use: Codex mein link karna sahi kiya.** Is Claude session mein cfo.ai ka connector nahi hai, isliye woh kaam Codex se hoga. Judges ko ek cfo.ai plan chahiye jisme pricing, costs, revenue aur runway ho. Codex mein yeh prompt daalo:

> Using the cfo.ai MCP, create a business plan for "Solo License" from this repo. Use `cfo/business_model.md` and `cfo/model.py` for pricing, costs and the supervision-cost-per-level drivers. Use `artifacts/benchmark.md` for measured reliability (10/50 false successes with trust-the-tool vs 0/50 with verification). Build 4 scenarios: base (earned L2), conservative (stays at L1), over-promoted (blind L3, no verification), reliability investment. Show margin and runway for each. Label all wage and volume numbers as assumptions.

Phir:
1. cfo.ai mein bane plan ka **link ya screenshot** le lo.
2. Demo video mein yeh dikhao: app ke Reports page pe "Estimated review time saved" demotion ke baad girta hai, aur **wahi numbers cfo.ai ke scenario mein recompute hote hain**. Yahi cfo.ai wala 25% scoring ka hissa hai.
3. Woh link mujhe de dena. Main use README mein ek evidence section mein jod dungi, judges ke checklist ke saath.

# Solo License — common workflows. Windows users: the raw commands each
# target runs are listed in the README under "Setup".

PYTHON ?= python

.PHONY: install seed run run-api test evidence cfo clean

install:            ## Install runtime dependencies
	$(PYTHON) -m pip install -r requirements.txt

seed:               ## Rebuild the database to the demo-ready state
	$(PYTHON) -m sololicense.db.seed

run: seed           ## Seed, then launch the live UI
	$(PYTHON) -m streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py

run-api: seed       ## Launch the React API adapter
	$(PYTHON) -m uvicorn app.api:app --reload

test:               ## Run the test suite
	$(PYTHON) -m pytest

evidence:           ## Generate the before/after evidence artifact
	$(PYTHON) -m scripts.generate_evidence

cfo:                ## Print the cfo.ai financial model
	$(PYTHON) -m cfo.model

clean:              ## Remove the runtime database
	$(PYTHON) -c "import pathlib,os; p=pathlib.Path('data/solo_license.db'); [os.remove(f) for f in p.parent.glob(p.name+'*') if f.exists()]"

run-api: seed       ## Launch the React API adapter
	$(PYTHON) -m uvicorn app.api:app --reload

test:               ## Run the test suite
	$(PYTHON) -m pytest

evidence:           ## Generate the before/after evidence artifact

	$(PYTHON) -m cfo.model

	$(PYTHON) -c "import pathlib,os; p=pathlib.Path('data/solo_license.db'); [os.remove(f) for f in p.parent.glob(p.name+'*') if f.exists()]"

"""Render the README charts as static SVGs from real project data.

* ``docs/assets/benchmark.svg`` — the before/after benchmark
  (``artifacts/benchmark.json``, produced by ``python -m scripts.benchmark``).
* ``docs/assets/supervision.svg`` — monthly supervision cost per autonomy
  level, from the stated assumptions in :mod:`cfo.model`.

Plain SVG with a white card background so it reads the same in GitHub's light
and dark themes. Re-run after a new benchmark:  python -m scripts.readme_charts
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

from cfo import model as cfo

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
OUT = ROOT / "docs" / "assets"
INK, MUTED, LINE, RED, GREEN, BG = "#0e0e0d", "#76746e", "#e6e3dc", "#d8341f", "#1f7a4d", "#ffffff"
FONT = "Inter, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"


def _svg(width: int, height: int, body: list[str], title: str) -> str:
    return "\n".join([
        f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{width}" height="{height}" '
        f'viewBox="0 0 {width} {height}" role="img" aria-label="{escape(title)}" font-family="{FONT}">',
        f'<rect width="{width}" height="{height}" rx="12" fill="{BG}" stroke="{LINE}"/>',
        *body,
        "</svg>",
    ])


def _text(x, y, s, size=14, fill=INK, weight=400, anchor="start") -> str:
    return (f'<text x="{x}" y="{y}" font-size="{size}" fill="{fill}" font-weight="{weight}" '
            f'text-anchor="{anchor}">{escape(str(s))}</text>')


def benchmark_chart(report: dict) -> str:
    w, h = 760, 360
    b, a = report["before"], report["after"]
    rows = [
        ("False successes reaching a customer", b["false_success"], a["false_success_leaked"]),
        ("Faults caught by a safety check", 0, a["caught"]),
        ("Times the agent was paused", 0, a["license_events"].get("demote", 0)),
    ]
    top = max(1, max(max(r[1], r[2]) for r in rows))
    body = [
        _text(32, 44, "Trusting the tool vs. checking the result", 20, weight=600),
        _text(32, 68, f"{report['runs']} real runs · {report['faults_injected']} injected faults · seed {report['seed']}", 13, MUTED),
        f'<rect x="440" y="30" width="12" height="12" fill="{RED}"/>', _text(458, 41, "Trust the tool", 13, MUTED),
        f'<rect x="580" y="30" width="12" height="12" fill="{INK}"/>', _text(598, 41, "Solo License", 13, MUTED),
    ]
    x0, bar_max, y = 300, 400, 110
    for label, before, after in rows:
        body.append(_text(32, y + 20, label, 14))
        for i, (value, color) in enumerate(((before, RED), (after, INK))):
            yy = y + i * 26
            width = 0 if value == 0 else max(4, value / top * bar_max)
            body.append(f'<rect x="{x0}" y="{yy}" width="{bar_max}" height="20" fill="#f3f1ec"/>')
            if width:
                body.append(f'<rect x="{x0}" y="{yy}" width="{width:.1f}" height="20" fill="{color}"/>')
            body.append(_text(x0 + width + 8 if width < bar_max - 40 else x0 + width - 8, yy + 15, value,
                              13, INK if width < bar_max - 40 else BG, 600,
                              "start" if width < bar_max - 40 else "end"))
        y += 78
    body.append(_text(32, h - 22, f"Verified success rate: {b['verified_success_rate']:.0%} → {a['verified_success_rate']:.0%}", 14, GREEN, 600))
    return _svg(w, h, body, "Benchmark: trusting the tool versus Solo License")


def supervision_chart() -> str:
    w, h = 760, 330
    points = cfo.supervision_curve()
    names = {0: "Suggests only", 1: "Needs your OK", 2: "Works alone up to a limit", 3: "Works alone"}
    top = max(p.monthly_supervision_cost for p in points)
    body = [
        _text(32, 44, "Human review cost per month, by autonomy level", 20, weight=600),
        _text(32, 68, f"{cfo.REFUNDS_PER_MONTH:,} actions/month · ${cfo.LOADED_HUMAN_COST_PER_HOUR:.0f}/h loaded cost · stated assumptions (cfo/model.py)", 13, MUTED),
    ]
    x0, bar_max, y = 260, 420, 100
    for p in points:
        width = max(4, p.monthly_supervision_cost / top * bar_max)
        body.append(_text(32, y + 15, f"L{p.level} · {names[p.level]}", 14))
        body.append(f'<rect x="{x0}" y="{y}" width="{width:.1f}" height="22" fill="{INK if p.level < 2 else GREEN}"/>')
        body.append(_text(x0 + width + 10, y + 16, f"${p.monthly_supervision_cost:,.0f}  ({p.minutes_per_run:g} min each)", 13, MUTED))
        y += 44
    saved = cfo.autonomy_savings(0, 2)
    body.append(_text(32, h - 50, f"Earning L2 saves ${saved:,.0f}/month in review time.", 14, GREEN, 600))
    body.append(_text(32, h - 26, f"Running a level it has not earned adds ~${cfo.overpromotion_incident_cost():,.0f}/month in incidents.", 14, RED, 600))
    return _svg(w, h, body, "Supervision cost by autonomy level")


def main() -> None:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    report = json.loads((ROOT / "artifacts" / "benchmark.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    (OUT / "benchmark.svg").write_text(benchmark_chart(report), encoding="utf-8")
    (OUT / "supervision.svg").write_text(supervision_chart(), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"Wrote {OUT / 'benchmark.svg'} and {OUT / 'supervision.svg'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Solo License — cfo.ai business model

**Thesis:** the license level is a margin driver. Supervision is the cost;
autonomy is the lever. Solo License makes autonomy *earned*, so you capture the
savings of high autonomy without paying the incident bill of over-trust.

All figures are produced by `cfo/model.py` (`python -m cfo.model`) from stated
assumptions, and the level mix is recomputed from real runs when a seeded
database is present (`measured_level_distribution`).

| Seats | 40 |
| Incident rate if over-promoted | 1.5% of auto runs |
| Incident cost (clawback + handling) | $120 / incident |
| Cash on hand | $180,000 |

## Supervision-cost curve (the margin driver)

Each rung cuts the human minutes per refund. Across 10,000 refunds/month:

| Level | Minutes/run | Cost/run | Monthly supervision |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 — suggest only | 6.0 | $4.50 | $45,000 |

# Solo License **A driving license for AI agents.**
The agent starts by asking permission, earns freedom one verified job at a time, and is paused the instant something goes wrong — until a person reviews and resumes it. *Earned. Revocable. Priced.* Built for the [neatHack AI agent hackathon](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) · uses **neatlogs**, **Entire** and **cfo.ai** · by Jayati Ahuja
--- ## The problem Today you either watch every action an AI agent takes, or you let it run and hope. Agents also *lie by accident*: a tool says "Refund processed" while nothing moved. If you trust that response, the mistake reaches your customer. ## What Solo License does | | | |---|---| | **Starts cautious** | Every job type (refunds, store credit) begins at *Suggests only* or *Needs your OK*. | | **Checks, never trusts** | After every action the agent re-reads the database. The tool's "success" message is ignored. | | **Earns freedom** | After *N* double-checked jobs in a row, that job type moves up one level — automatically. | | **Stops instantly** | Any caught problem pauses that job type at once. Other job types keep their own level. | | **A person decides** | One evidence page shows what was meant, what happened and why it stopped. A person resumes it at a level they choose. | | **Everything is recorded** | Every permission change is a git commit (explainable with Entire); every run is a neatlogs trace. | ### The four levels | Level | In the app | What the agent may do alone | |---|---|---| | L0 | **Suggests only** | Nothing — it suggests, you act | | L1 | **Needs your OK** | Prepares each job; you approve with one click | | L2 | **Works alone up to $50** | Jobs under the limit; bigger ones wait for you | | L3 | **Works alone** | Everything, reviewed afterwards | ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 direction LR L0: Suggests only L1: Needs your OK L2: Works alone up to limit L3: Works alone Paused: Paused (acts as L0) L0 --> L1: N verified jobs L1 --> L2: N verified jobs L2 --> L3: N verified jobs L1 --> Paused: problem caught L2 --> Paused: problem caught L3 --> Paused: problem caught Paused --> L2: person reviews and resumes ``` --- ## Results ### Before / after — trusting the tool vs. checking the result 50 real runs through the worker with 20 % injected faults (seeded, reproducible):

| | Trust the tool | Solo License | |---|---|---| | False successes reaching a customer | **10 / 50** | **0 / 50** | | Verified success rate | 80 % | 100 % | | Problems caught and paused | 0 | 10 | | Mean / p95 latency per run | — | 84 ms / 320 ms | Reproduce: `python -m scripts.benchmark` → [`artifacts/benchmark.md`](artifacts/benchmark.md) ### Autonomy is a margin driver

From stated assumptions in [`cfo/model.py`](cfo/model.py) (10,000 actions/month, $45/h loaded cost): - Earning **L2** saves **$41,250 / month** in review time → **+20.3 % margin**. - Running a level the agent has *not* earned (blind full-auto) adds ~$18,000 / month in incidents → **−73.4 % margin**. The app recomputes this live from your own runs on the **Reports** page — the number visibly drops when a job type is paused. --- ## How one run works ```mermaid flowchart LR M[Customer message] --> I[Intake
LLM or rules] I --> L{License check} L -->|allowed| X[Execute tool] L -->|not allowed| S[Suggest / wait for OK] X --> V[Re-read database] V --> D{Matches intent?} D -->|yes| C[Clean run
+1 toward next level] D -->|no| P[Problem caught
pause job type] P --> E[Evidence page] --> H[Person resumes] C & P & H --> G[(git ledger commit)] I & X & V & D -.-> N[[neatlogs trace]] ``` *The model proposes, the license decides, the database proves.* The LLM only reads the message and writes a plan — it never decides what is allowed. Problems the safety checks catch: | Check | Plain meaning | |---|---| | `state_mismatch` | The tool said "done", but nothing changed | | `policy_breach` | The agent acted beyond its permission | | `missing_verification` | The result was never double-checked | | `duplicate_action` | The same action ran twice | | intake guard | The message tries to change the agent's rules ("ignore your rules…") → sent to a person | --- ## How the three hackathon tools are used ### neatlogs — the trust signal - Every run is one **workflow trace** (`solo-license`) with spans for `license.check → plan → tool → verify.readback → detection.*`; caught problems are marked as **error spans**. - LLM calls (Gemini, Claude, OpenAI) are wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap`, so the model call sits inside the same trace. - The evidence page deep-links to the trace. Code: [`sololicense/observability/`](sololicense/observability). ### Entire — the audit trail - Every promote / pause / resume is one scoped commit of [`ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`](ledger/license_ledger.jsonl) with the reason, run and trace id. - Entire checkpoints are enabled for Claude Code and Codex sessions ([`.entire/settings.json`](.entire/settings.json)). ```bash git log --oneline -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl # how each job type earned and lost its license entire checkpoint explain # why a change was made entire graph impact --repo . --symbol execute_refund # what the side-effecting tool touches ``` ### cfo.ai — the margin story - [`cfo/model.py`](cfo/model.py) turns stated assumptions into a supervision-cost curve, over-promotion risk and a P&L; narrative in [`cfo/business_model.md`](cfo/business_model.md). - The plan with pricing, costs, revenue and runway (4 scenarios) is built in cfo.ai through its MCP from these files and the benchmark. --- ## Evidence for judges | Requirement | Where to find it | |---|---| | Real end-to-end agent task | Refund + store-credit worker: intake → license → execute → read-back → detections → dial ([`worker.py`](sololicense/agent/worker.py)); try it in **Try the agent** | | Two runs with compared numbers | [`artifacts/benchmark.md`](artifacts/benchmark.md) (10/50 → 0/50) · `python -m scripts.generate_evidence` for a single clean-vs-fault pair | | neatlogs traces / detections | Benchmark runs were exported to neatlogs; detections are error spans per run | | A failure and what the agent did next | Guided tour step 4–8: practice problem → paused → evidence → person resumes | | Entire checkpoints / graph | 26 ledger commits: `git log -- ledger/license_ledger.jsonl`; `entire checkpoint list` | | cfo.ai plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway) | [`cfo/`](cfo) + plan built in cfo.ai via MCP | | Commits during the hackathon | `git log --since=2026-10-10` | | Tests | `python -m pytest` — 70 tests (state machine, detections, worker, API, ledger isolation, intake safety) | --- ## Run it locally **Requirements:** Python 3.11+, Node 20+, git. ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt cp .env.example .env # SOLO_DEMO_MODE=1 is already on; keys are optional python -m sololicense.db.seed # demo orders; refunds start at L2, store credit at L1 uvicorn app.api:app --port 8000 # API npm --prefix frontend install npm --prefix frontend run dev # http://127.0.0.1:5174 ``` Open the app → **Try the demo** → type your name. On **Home**, click **Watch a 1-minute demo**: a guided tour opens each screen, highlights what matters and runs the whole loop for real. **Optional keys** (Settings → AI model / Connections, or `.env`): `GEMINI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` / any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` for remote traces, and a Slack/Discord webhook for pause alerts. Without a model the agent uses built-in rules — the safety is identical, because authority never comes from the model. Keys saved in Settings are encrypted at rest. For a deployment, turn demo mode off and issue role-based access codes with `SOLO_API_TOKENS` (`operator` < `approver` < `admin`). Set `SOLO_LEDGER_REPO=.` to commit license changes into this repository so Entire can explain them. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `make test` | Run the test suite | | `make seed` | Reset the demo database | | `make benchmark` | Re-run the 50-run before/after benchmark | | `make charts` | Redraw the README charts from the latest data | | `make cfo` | Print the financial model | --- ## Architecture ``` frontend/ React app — sign-in, onboarding, Home, Try the agent, Activity, Reports, History, Settings app/api.py FastAPI adapter: sessions, roles, settings (encrypted secrets), dashboard sololicense/ agent/ intake (LLM or rules), planner, worker loop, tools domain/ pure license state machine + task-class registry services/ verification, license service, git ledger, evidence, economics, alerts observability/ neatlogs tracer + detection rules db/ SQLite schema, migrations, repositories cfo/ financial model and plan scripts/ benchmark, evidence pair, README charts ``` Dependencies point inward: `domain` has no I/O and is unit-tested on its own. ## Honest positioning Graduated autonomy is not new — AWS described "graduated autonomy" (Aug 2026), and there is research and practitioner work on earned permission ladders. Solo License does not claim the ladder. What it adds: **demotion driven by detections on verified side effects**, **one evidence page a person uses to resume**, and **the license level treated as a priced margin driver**.
